prompt:
INPUT: the attached image is the approved character — her Fantasy card; keep her. Do not reuse earlier conversation images.

CHARACTER: the same woman as the attached image — the personification of Graphite, of the Carbon Nation, seen in her everyday life. Keep her face, eye and hair colors, haircut, skin tone and body proportions; expression and hair motion may change, and her hair may be worn differently only as SCENE's Hair line says. The substance shows ONLY as a small accessory, an object around her, or the object PROP says she holds — never in the outfit's colours, patterns or cut, never as armor, regalia or a costume.

DESIGN (accessory hints only): her element's visual language — two faces of one element: black soot and clear diamond; hexagonal lattices (graphite, graphene) as patterns, pencil-graphite grey, carbon-fibre weave; it bonds with everything and is the frame of all life — may inform at most one small accessory, a hair ornament or an object beside her, in its palette (charcoal black, graphite grey, diamond white, a single living green). The clothes keep the chosen outfit's own colours; her skin, hair and eyes stay as in the attached image.

STYLE: Polished 2.5D game key art with clean linework, anime facial design that keeps each character's own facial structure, eye proportions and skin tone instead of one house face, layered cel-to-soft shading and crisp fabric and accessory detail. Use a vivid, readable silhouette and natural lighting.

AGE: the same adult woman as in the attached image — keep her own face shape, cheekbones, eye proportions and skin tone exactly; minimal facial lines (no nasolabial folds, crow's feet, under-eye bags or cheek creases).

OUTPUT: one standalone off-duty scene of her in the outfit chosen in SCENE; her element shows only through accessories and objects around her — never in the outfit's colours, patterns or cut, never as armor, regalia or a costume. Everything else follows SCENE (chosen).

FRAME: a vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) image. Compose the image for this frame; COMPOSITION in SCENE sets how much of her shows.

WORLD: this scene happens inside her own kingdom, the Carbon Nation, as if she simply lives there — a charcoal-burner's forest and a diamond mine: hexagonal crystal caves, smoking charcoal kilns, a world tree with lattice-patterned bark. Its architecture, props, light and weather show the world; no creatures, no second character, no readable text other than her element's own symbol and atomic number. Her clothes stay the everyday outfit SCENE describes, not regalia or armor.

SCENE (chosen):
Place: an inn or tavern of her element's kingdom at night, a counter and a fire
Outfit: a striped cotton peshtemal wrapped like a dress
POSTURE: standing at a waist-high railing or sill, leaning lightly on it.
COMPOSITION: an environmental long shot, her complete figure and enough of the place around her; body turned three-quarters away from the camera; head turned back over her shoulder; camera at her eye level.
Lens / perspective: 35mm-equivalent environmental perspective balancing the woman and the setting with moderate depth.
RIGHT HAND: her own right hand rests on the railing.
LEFT HAND: her own left hand tucks hair behind her ear.
LEGS: weight on one leg, the other knee softly bent.
GAZE: she looks into the camera.
EXPRESSION: heavy-lidded eyes, lips slightly parted and relaxed, brow smooth.
overall_intensity: strong — maximal styling presence within the scene; retain chosen exposure and anatomy
skin_exposure: bold — more scene-appropriate shoulder, back, midriff or leg exposure; cover chest and pelvis

WARDROBE: change her clothes completely. From the attached image take only her face, hair and body — not its garment, armor, regalia, ornaments, mecha plates or background. Dress her exactly as SCENE describes; that outfit must read at first glance, keeping its own recognisable colours and parts. Do not carry the attached image's palette, patterns or trim into the outfit; her element belongs in accessories and props, never in the clothes — never restyle the chosen outfit into her element's palette, materials, patterns or regalia.

ANGLE: the attached image fixes who she is, not how she is posed or shot. Do not copy its head angle, head tilt, gaze direction, face size in frame, camera height or crop — turn her head, set her gaze and place the camera exactly as SCENE describes, and let her face read naturally from that new angle (profile, three-quarter, looking down or away), with her features staying the same. No default card pose, no default front-facing portrait.

LOOK-BACK: her back is toward the camera and her head turns at most a quarter turn over one shoulder — the face shows in profile or three-quarter view, never full-front on a back-facing torso. Her chin sits just above the near shoulder, the far eye and cheek may be partly hidden, the side of the neck shows the turn and the shoulder line continues behind the head. Where her eyes go follows GAZE.

ONE MAIN FIGURE: she is the only character in focus. Where the place is busy, other people may appear only as small, soft-focus background extras — never posed with her. No logo, no watermark, no speech bubble, no frame border. No text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (C) and atomic number (6) — those two may appear readably (engraved, stamped, glowing or on a sign or label); nothing else is written.

ANATOMY: natural adult proportions, about 7.5 heads tall — height from the legs, never a smaller head or a longer neck. The neck is a natural length and the head sits close to the shoulders. No body-part enlargement, no extra limbs.

BODY: a normal human body — one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; elbows, knees and wrists bend the human way. Hands and feet may be partly hidden by the pose, what she holds or the frame. Right and left mean her own right and left, not the viewer's.

HANDS: natural human hands, no extra or duplicated limbs; each visible hand joins through its wrist and forearm to the matching shoulder. A hand may stay outside the crop, and fingers may be partly hidden by a grip.

Output exactly 1024 x 1536. The ONLY correction is her extra third arm: on the VIEWER'S LEFT of her torso, directly underneath the long hanging hair, a stray pale forearm descends vertically to the railing at approximately x=340, y=630–700 in this 1024x1536 image. Remove that entire stray forearm/hand, and restore the hair/background/railing naturally in its place. Keep exactly TWO arms: the existing near arm extending diagonally down toward VIEWER'S RIGHT, with its hand resting on the railing at x=805,y=700; and the existing bent raised arm whose hand touches her hair beside her head at x=585,y=215. Keep the raised arm naturally connected to the far shoulder and the railing arm naturally connected to the near shoulder. No third shoulder, arm, elbow, wrist or hand anywhere. Two natural human hands, five fingers each, with natural occlusion. Preserve everything else, including the woman's face and pose, without changing outfit or exposure.
